basis: Big Lots publicly confirmed the threshold crossing on May 27, 2022. Fiscal Q1 2022 consolidated net sales were $1,374,714,000 versus $1,625,552,000 a year earlier, below the $1,544,274,400 cutoff. The March 3 outlook already implied a decline of roughly 8.7% even at the favorable end, but Big Lots gave separate comparable-sales and store-growth assumptions without stating a consolidated revenue ceiling. I could verify the written conference materials but could not verify the full January 11 and March 9 public management remarks. That gap leaves the earliest qualifying date unresolved.

coverage.detail: December 3, 2021, preceding earnings cycle. The Q3 release guided Q4 FY2021 comparable sales and EPS. Its expectation of record FY2022 sales applied to the full year.

December 3 call. The CFO identified Q1 FY2022 as the toughest stimulus comparison. His five-point estimate measured the prior stimulus benefit to full-year comparable sales. He gave no Q1 consolidated sales bound.

January 10 business update. The $8 billion to $10 billion sales goal was long-term. The trading update covered Q4 FY2021. Big Lots announced a January 11 public fireside chat and said its replay would be available through January 21.
The January ICR investor deck presented long-term financial goals. I found no Q1 FY2022 consolidated revenue ceiling in the deck and could not verify the full accompanying spoken remarks.

March 3 Q4 FY2021 release. For Q1 FY2022, management translated approximately 10% comparable-sales growth versus 2019 into a low-double-digit comparable-sales decline versus 2021. The $1.10 to $1.20 range was diluted EPS.

March 3 presentation, slide 21. Both assumptions explicitly covered Q1 FY2022. Taking 10% as the smallest double-digit comparable-sales decline and adding the projected 1.3 percentage points from net new and relocated stores gives approximately −8.7% year over year. This is a calculated implication of the outlook. The slide gives no explicit high endpoint for consolidated net sales.

The CFO repeated the Q1 comparable-sales outlook and described the contribution from new and relocated stores as roughly 130 basis points. The issuer’s covering 8-K confirms the call took place March 3, 2022.

Outside EDGAR, the issuer’s newswire listing identifies a March 4 announcement of its March 9 Bank of America conference appearance and a May 13 notice scheduling results for May 27. I found no intervening written Q1 consolidated sales preannouncement and could not verify a complete public record of the March 9 remarks.

May 27 actual results. The net-sales row for the quarters ended April 30, 2022 and May 1, 2021 gives 1,374,714 and 1,625,552, respectively, in thousands of dollars. Big Lots reported a 15.4% consolidated decline, a 17.0% comparable-sales decline and approximately 1.6 percentage points of growth from net new stores and relocations.

publication_date_evidence: Big Lots’ March 8-K confirms it released earnings, held the call and directed investors to the published deck on March 3, 2022. Its May 8-K confirms it released Q1 actuals on May 27, 2022. The issuer’s wire release timestamps those results at 6:00 a.m. ET.
